bullets.text: Operating income rose to $220.1M ($2.84/share); net income was $250.5M ($3.24/share); ROE 19.6% vs 27.4% in 1994; underwriting margin was 5.7% (5.2% core), exceeding the 4% target.
Total NPW grew 19% YOY to $2,912.8M without additional debt or equity financing; core business NPW increased 21% to $2,824.2M, representing 97% of companywide net premiums written.

Total portfolio reached $3,768.0M with 12.4% taxable equivalent return; debt-to-capital fell to 31%; NPW to statutory surplus was 2.8:1; all held-to-maturity investments were reclassified as available-for-sale.
Underwriting expenses dropped 1.7 percentage points to 22% of premiums, down from 24% in 1994 and 32% in 1990; steady cost reduction remains a core pillar alongside Gainsharing incentives.
Ranked as the 7th largest U.S. private passenger auto insurer with a 2.6% market share; expanding beyond nonstandard auto into the approximately $81B standard and preferred auto market.

Over 30,000 independent agencies serve as the primary distribution method; offering standard and preferred auto helps agents regain market share, complemented by national accounts and direct phone channels.
1-800-AUTO-PRO telephone shopping service uses TV and direct mail, providing consumers 15-minute comparative rate quotes against up to three competitors, including State Farm and Allstate.
Offers pricing to every licensed driver; standard and preferred volume grew to 5–10% of 1995 premium; monitoring each program to adjust rates promptly to sustain the 4% target margin.

Established World Wide Web presence on April 7, 1995 at auto-insurance.com, becoming the first major insurer online; site provides financial info, safety material, and comparative rates from four insurers.

Gainsharing represented 9.4% of total 1995 compensation. Progressive emphasized Total Quality Management, concluded countrywide community management best supports its goals, and aimed for new hires to reflect local demographics.
